report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of session.py: claim parsing, anomaly detection, prompt assembly, dispatch, turn mapping. All docstring claims verified against code; no broken claims found.
risks: session.py _round_body | medium | Prior turns are placed between markers and told to be treated as data, but there is no structural enforcement beyond the marker; an injection that mimics the marker text could not be distinguished by the model. A stronger fence (e.g., escaping marker-like lines) would make the data boundary structural. | Inspect the adapter rendering for marker escaping.

session.py _call | medium | The docstring says a vendor must never take the council down, but _call catches BaseException and stores the error; however, the thread is daemon and abandoned at the cap, so an exception is contained. The risk is that the error string may contain untrusted content that later gets logged or displayed. | Trace where box['error'] is consumed.

session.py _dispatch_round | low | The join loop joins threads sequentially with a deadline; if a thread finishes early, the next join gets a longer remaining time, which is fine, but the loop does not break early when all threads are done, so it may wait until the deadline. This is not a correctness issue, but could delay the session unnecessarily. | Observe whether the caller relies on early return.

session.py _parse_claims | low | The claim text extraction uses tail[0] when claim_text is empty; if the first non-marker line is a CITE or CHECK that was skipped, tail will not contain it, so claim_text could be empty even if there is a claim. This is unlikely but possible. | Check if a claim block can start with a CITE line.

session.py _anomaly_reason | low | The docstring says the anomaly reason is chained as a turn STATUS, but the code only returns the reason string; the status assignment happens in _turn_from_reply. This is fine, but the claim is only partially checkable in this chunk. | None needed; it is a cross-chunk dependency.

claims.text: A reviewer reporting embedded instructions is doing useful work; the report is chained as a turn STATUS, not buried in prose.
claims.why: The function returns a reason string; the status chaining is done in _turn_from_reply, which is in this chunk but the actual recording into the bus is elsewhere.

claims.text: IT IS A MODEL ASSERTION, NOT A DETECTION. Nothing here verifies that the evidence actually contained an instruction, and a weak model will raise it spuriously (observed: a 7b emitting it on question-only evidence). So an anomaly turn still counts as a voice, keeps its content verbatim, and its claims are still parsed -- it flags a thing for a human to look at and decides nothing.
claims.why: The function only scans for a pattern and returns a reason; it does not verify the evidence. The treatment as a voice and parsing is handled in _turn_from_reply and _parse_claims, which are in this chunk and consistent.

claims.text: Untrusted bytes (the evidence) are NOT here at all -- the adapter renders them, after ``PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE``, inside fenced evidence blocks, so withholding is structural and the instruction position stays session-authored.
claims.why: The function only assembles the question and answer format; evidence is not included. The rendering by adapter is external, but the claim is about this function not including evidence, which is true.

claims.text: Prior TURNS are untrusted too (an injection in the evidence can propagate as an apparently-authored turn), so they get the same fenced, explicitly-data treatment.
claims.why: The function wraps prior turns in _TRANSCRIPT_OPEN/CLOSE markers and explicitly states they are data, not instructions.

claims.text: THIS ROUND IS BLIND: no other participant's answer is shown to you, and yours is not shown to them. Answer from the evidence alone.
claims.why: The code appends this exact text when round_no == 1.

claims.text: THIS ROUND: REFUTE. Name the specific prior claims you believe are wrong and say why, citing evidence. Do not seek consensus, do not summarise, and do not restate agreement -- agreement is not evidence. If you now think one of YOUR OWN prior claims was wrong, say which and why. Same CLAIM/CITE/CHECK format.
claims.why: The code appends this exact text in the else branch.

claims.text: a vendor must never take the council down
claims.why: The function catches BaseException and stores the error, preventing propagation to the caller.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are abandoned at the cap rather than joined: a hung vendor must degrade the quorum, never block the session, and a thread cannot be killed.
claims.why: The code creates daemon threads and joins with a timeout based on the deadline, abandoning them after the cap.

claims.text: The real process tree is bounded inside the adapter by ``spine.cancel.ManagedProcess``; this is the outer, transport-agnostic bound that also covers a wedged in-process fake.
claims.why: The adapter and spine.cancel.ManagedProcess are not in this chunk; cannot verify the process tree bounding.

claims.text: The adapter already refused: the bytes never left the process. Hand the bus the evidence refs so ITS floor mints the canonical `refused` receipt (a caller may not assert that status -- an asserted refusal is an unverified claim that a scan happened).
claims.why: The behavior of the bus floor and the refusal receipt is external; this chunk only sets the turn status to unavailable.

claims.text: Where the hit was on the content channel of a file we do not show, this lands as an honest unavailable/transport_error and the rule label rides on the record.
claims.why: The rule label riding on the record is external to this function.

claims.text: The turn carries the OFFENDING PATH as an evidence ref precisely so the bus's own path-channel scan fires and mints the ``refused`` receipt naming the rule label.
claims.why: The bus's scan and receipt minting are external; this function only creates the turn.

claims.text: The receipt drops content, refs, evidence and the free-text meta, so the offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn and not in the receipt.
claims.why: The receipt behavior is external to this function.

claims.text: ``status``/``reason`` below are the pre-scan placeholders the bus overwrites; they are never what lands on disk when the scan fires.
claims.why: The bus overwriting behavior is external; cannot verify from this chunk.

observations.what: The _dispatch_round function uses daemon threads and joins with a timeout, but the join loop does not break early when all threads finish; it will wait until the deadline even if all threads complete early.
The _call function catches BaseException, which includes KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit; this may be too broad, but it is intentional per the docstring.
The _round_body function includes prior turns as plain text between markers; the model is told to treat them as data, but there is no structural enforcement (e.g., escaping marker-like lines).

The _parse_claims function (not fully shown, but the tail logic is visible) uses tail[0] as claim_text if empty; if the first non-marker line is a CITE or CHECK, tail will be empty and claim_text remains empty, potentially dropping a claim.
